title: Where the Speed Went
author: Nadina Dorene Lisbon
summary: In this TechSips issue Nadina Lisbon asks where the time goes when AI makes people faster. She reads a Gallup survey in which 63 percent of AI users say they work faster but only 47 percent say they get more time on interesting work, and 31 percent say their employer has asked them to take on more. Workday job-posting data suggests more airtime for building with AI and less for management and training skills, and Challenger data shows AI cited in about 9 percent of September job cuts. The practical exercise asks a manager to review the last three times they added to a direct report's plate and note whether 'they're faster now' played a part. The big idea uses the 38 years between Francis Halzen's neutrino proposal and his Nobel Prize to argue that patient work such as growing a manager compounds more than quick output. The closing question is what long-horizon work a leader would protect with some of the speed.
points: Self-reported survey data shows AI's speed appears more readily than better work or more time for interesting tasks.
A five-step audit of your last three asks to a direct report reveals whether added work was a choice or a habit.
The phrase 'get more out of the employees we already have' can mean more volume or more of what people can become, and speed does not choose between them.
Work that compounds in an organization, like growing a manager, runs on a much longer clock than AI-accelerated tasks.
quotes: Postings are giving more airtime to building with AI and less to the people who help others grow into it.
These are the reasons companies give, so they tell us how decisions are being described more than what’s driving them.
Scroll your sent messages, chat, or 1:1 notes and find the last three times you added something to a direct report’s plate.
The work that compounds in an organization tends to look more like IceCube. Growing a manager. Moving someone into a role they weren’t quite ready for last year.

I find that phrase interesting because it can mean two very different things. “More out of” can mean more volume from the same people. It can also mean more of what those people are capable of becoming.
The speed doesn’t choose between those. We do, usually one small request at a time.
